Please, please, please.....Where are all of the Internal Rate of Return nerds?

This virtual session is for you!

Starting at 4am, that was not a typo (don't worry if that is too early, you can register for the replay).

Looking for like minded IRR enthusias that want to make history by attending the first event of New York Tech week. 

There's something special about being first that is oh so sweet. 

Running for only 30 minutes (so you can go back to sleep if needed) this session will cover 3 of the most important IRRs (there are over 15).

The IRRs covered are:
Modified IRR ✔️ 
Time Zero IRR ✔️ 
De-annualized IRR ✔️ 

Last year tech week I hosted the miseducation of IRR and that event was a blast so I'm looking to do things a little different and kick start tech week with the first event happening. 

For those of you not familiar with IRR, IRR or Internal Rate of Return is the famous (or infamous depending on who you talk to) calculation that is used to evaluate Venture Capital and Private Equity Returns.

Despite having it's weaknesses, the calculation is fraught with it's avid users in the Private Capital Markets.  

So grab your coffee, tea or matcha and attend the first event of New York tech week. 

Note a recap will be emailed to all those who cannot make it as some attendees are bound to oversleep given the time. 

The recap/replay will be available during the entire text week for you to enjoy.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com

*Please allow 12-72 hours for approval.

partiful-wazzojiazjipjfmyrgps.description:
A joint event with One Health Collective & NXGN, hosted by Scalpels & Spreadsheets.

Agenda:
Doors Open: 10.55AM
Session 1:  11.00 - 12.00PM
Session 2: 12.00PM - 1.00PM
Networking: 1.00 - 1.30PM 
_______________________________

Session One | One Health Collective (11-12)

Patients are no longer starting their healthcare journey inside the health system.

From wearables + labs, DTC care delivery, and AI-native care platforms, consumers are increasingly building their own front door to healthcare.

Health systems are responding, but the behavior shift is already underway.

- How do health systems view  the rise of consumer health, wearables, DTC labs, and AI guidance/doctors. 

- How forward-thinking health systems are rebuilding patient access, management, and engagement

- What healthcare organizations can’t afford to get wrong with these shifts underway

Speakers:

Dr. Devin Mann, Director of the Section of Digitally Enabled Care (SoDEC) at NYU Langone Health, leading cross-disciplinary teams across digital health research, operations, and innovation. He also directs FuturePractice, NYU Langone's internal tech innovation lab, and serves as Strategic Director of Digital Health Innovation within Health Informatics.

Daniel Marchalik, MD, MBA, Medical Director of Business Innovation and Executive Director of the MedStar Health Center for Wellbeing, leading venture, commercialization, and IP strategy at MedStar Health, the largest integrated health system in the Mid-Atlantic.

Holden Groves, MD, an anesthesiologist and critical care physician at Columbia University, where his clinical work spans the operating room and ICU. He also leads inpatient AI and mobile solutions at NewYork-Presbyterian, building the tools that bring emerging technology to the bedside across one of the country's largest health systems.

Co-Moderators:

John Joshua, RRT, MHA : Co- Founder, One Health Collective 

Addison Montiel, RN, MBA : Co- Founder, One Health Collective 
_______________________________

Session Two | NXGN (12-1)

Patients are arriving with lab panels, wearable data, GLP-1s, peptide protocols, and AI-assisted self-diagnosis already in hand.

What does that mean for the clinicians now treating them?

- Physicians on the front lines of consumer health and self-directed care

- GLP-1s, peptides, optimization culture, and the informed patient

- What medicine looks like when the patient journey starts before the clinic does

Speakers:

David Kessler, MD, MSc is the Vice Chair of Innovation and Professor of Pediatrics in Emergency Medicine at Columbia University, leads strategic cross-disciplinary initiatives focused on designing, testing, and implementing emerging technologies to improve healthcare training and clinical care. His work spans artificial intelligence, simulation, ultrasound, and immersive technologies. He has led multi-center research collaborations, authored over 200 peer-reviewed publications, and co-founded INSPIRE, an international network advancing innovation and scholarship in simulation science.

George Matthew, MD, MBA, FACP is a practicing Internal Medicine physician with over two decades of corporate and startup experience, including GE, Goldman Sachs, Pfizer, Medidata Solutions, Aetna, and served as the Chief Medical Officer of Hewlett Packard, later DXC Technology.  While practicing he also serves as the Chief Medical Officer of Times AI Health, a privacy-based health chatbot startup. 

Peter Rezkalla, MD, known to millions as "Doctor Disney," is a practicing pediatrician specializing in Pediatrics, Public Health, and Mental Health, as well as an award-winning child advocate spearheading the new era of health education for families and global communities. Leveraging his training in both medicine and musical theater, he transforms healthcare through creativity, tech, and story-driven science. With over 200 million views on social media, he is a top-trusted voice among healthcare leaders today.

Moderators:

Aakash Saraiya: Emergency Medicine Physician, Investor and Co-Chair of NXGN


This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

Artificial intelligence is transforming drug discovery and clinical medicine - but AI is only as powerful as the data underlying it. The next frontier is not bigger datasets: it is spatially resolved datasets. Spatial multi-omics technologies can now simultaneously capture gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and protein abundance with precise X-Y tissue coordinates, creating a new class of tissue-level foundation models that transcend models based on bulk and single-cell data.

This panel brings together five leading scientists and technologists from Yale, Columbia, IAS Princeton, and KAUST to explore a pivotal question: How will spatial multi-omics reshape AI models for disease treatment across diverse ancestral backgrounds, and accelerate drug discovery from target identification to clinical validation?

Build Your First AI Voice Agent
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how humans interact with technology, and voice agents are emerging as one of the most powerful interfaces for AI applications. This workshop introduces developers to the foundations of agentic voice systems and shows how to build intelligent voice agents capable of interacting with users in real time.

Sponsored by Cloudonix, this hands-on demonstration workshop explores how developers can combine modern AI models with real-time voice infrastructure to create practical applications such as AI receptionists, automated service agents, and conversational assistants.

During the session, participants will learn how to use Dograh, an open-source framework for building agentic voice systems, together with the programmable voice infrastructure provided by Cloudonix.

What You’ll Learn
Participants will be introduced to the core components of an AI voice agent, including:
• How agentic AI systems interact with voice interfaces
 • The architecture of modern AI voice bots
 • Connecting AI models to real-time voice communication
 • Building a functional voice agent using open tools
 • Rapid prototyping techniques for voice-based applications

The workshop will include live demonstrations showing how a developer can go from concept to a working voice agent using open-source tools and cloud communications APIs.

Who Should Attend
This workshop is designed for:
• University students studying computer science or AI
 • Recent graduates interested in AI startups
 • Developers exploring conversational AI
 • Entrepreneurs interested in voice-enabled applications

What Participants Receive
All registered participants will receive three months of free access to Cloudonix services, enabling them to continue building and experimenting with their own voice agents after the event.
The location will be provided to registered attendees.

Duration
3-hour


This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

Age and Identity verification is full of deepfakes. It is getting harder and harder to distinguish honest actors from fraudsters. 

The solution isn't that we use better AI tools to detect deepfakes - that is playing a losing battle. Rather we should be using authoritative sources and cryptography to verify user's identity. 

That is what Reclaim Protocol does (https://reclaimprotocol.org) - an open source verification system that uses zero knowledge proofs to verify users' identity. 

Come learn more, and discuss with others solving the same problem. Each participant will be hand picked, to maintain high density of like minded people. 

Looking forward to seeing you!

Raising a Series A is a fundamentally different process than raising a seed round. Expectations shift—from vision to execution, from storytelling to metrics, and from promise to proof. This panel is designed for seed-stage founders who want a clear, realistic view of what it takes to successfully raise a Series A in today’s market.

You’ll hear directly from industry professionals as to what Series A VCs actually look for, how founders derail otherwise strong raises, and how to prepare months in advance—not weeks.

Target Audience:
- Seed-stage founders planning to raise a Series A in the next 6–18 months
- Founders who have product-market fit signals but want clarity on readiness
- CEOs navigating early traction, hiring, and go-to-market scale
Founders who want to avoid common Series A fundraising mistakes

Topics of Discussion:
- What “Series A ready” really means in 2026 (metrics, momentum, narrative)?
- What are the key diligence questions Series A investors focus on and why, including pre-raise legal and financial considerations?
- How Series A expectations differ from seed across product, GTM, and team?
-How does a founder run a tight Series A process (timing, data room, investor targeting)?
- Valuation, ownership, and control considerations founders often overlook when raising their first priced round.

New York Tech Week is loud, fast, and technical. Before you dive in, come find your people to help you navigate this week with social good in mind.

AI is reshaping every sector that touches social impact such as and not exclusive: climate, health, education, conservation, and capital. But the most important conversations aren't happening on stages. They're happening between the people doing the work: the researchers, founders, funders, advocates, and practitioners who are navigating real tradeoffs, in real communities, with real stakes.

This is an open, informal gathering at The Globe Bar to kick off Tech Week with intention. Come ready to talk about how we use AI and tech safely, responsibly, and sustainably  and what it means to build technology that actually serves people.

This is a meetup, there are no panels, but rather structured networking where you’ll break into groups of what you are interested in and meet people similar to collaborate and brainstorm with.

Who should come: Social impact enthusiasts. Climate tech builders and ocean conservationists. Nonprofit leaders. Impact investors and philanthropists. Global health advocates and humanitarian responders. Community organizers and policy thinkers. Anyone who wants to walk into Tech Week thinking about what technology should actually be for.

This event is a part of #NYCTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.


Hosts:
Paulina Muñoz is the author of Do Good Capital, a newsletter at the intersection of technology, investing, culture, and social impact, rooted in a deep belief that the financial system is one of the most powerful levers for social change. Her path from international policy to investment banking at HSBC and now to venture capital — where she spent time with Equal Opportunity Ventures as an investment fellow backing companies serving low-income and historically marginalized communities — has given her a rare, cross-sector view of how capital can be redirected toward the communities that need it most.

Angela Ng is the Director of Business Innovation at Carnegie Mellon University, where she has spent nearly five years leading sustainability, AI, and innovation programs across CMU's global campuses. With a decade of international development experience, spanning water and sanitation in Bangladesh and the DRC, maternal and child health in India, and disaster resilience across Africa and the Middle East, she brings a grounded, field-tested lens to emerging technology. She is passionate about responsible AI adoption in the social sector and is actively exploring how AI can drive climate action, ocean conservation, and equitable access at scale. She believes the most important work happens at the edges of disciplines, not the center of any one field. She is a Globethics AI Governance Fellow for 2026, focusing on AI ethics standards in Global South contexts.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com

partiful-8hy03hoeb7xdq7j3rc7b.description:
Where will climate and deep tech actually scale—and with whom?
As AI-driven energy demand accelerates and geopolitical shifts reshape global supply chains, investor focus is moving toward one critical question: which markets, platforms, and partnerships can turn innovation into real-world deployment.
At the same time, cities and states across the U.S. are taking on a more decisive role in shaping the conditions for that deployment. Governors in 24 states—representing approximately 60% of the U.S. economy and 55% of its population—remain committed to climate action, while 46 states and more than 350 cities continue to advance local initiatives. Beyond federal policy, these subnational dynamics are becoming increasingly central.
In parallel, attention is turning to partners capable of supporting the transition from proof of concept to commercialization. Japan, with its deep industrial base, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and global corporate networks, is emerging as a critical partner in enabling large-scale deployment—particularly in sectors such as energy systems, infrastructure, and materials.
This event will convene investors from the U.S. and Japan, along with policymakers and industry leaders, to share insights on these trends from a U.S.–Japan investor perspective, and to explore where and how the next phase of scaling will take place through emerging opportunities for U.S.–Japan collaboration.

Overview
	Date: Monday, June 1st
	Time: Doors open at 2:30 PM. The session will take place from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM, including a networking segment.
	Venue: Baker & McKenzie LLP (452 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10018)
	Format: Invitation-only (Up to 130 participants)
	Initiated by: City of Yokohama, Greennex Global, ShibuLA Ventures
	Venue Sponsored by: Baker & McKenzie LLP
	Tea Sponsored by: ITO EN
	In Partnership with: Deep Tech Forum

Program Detail（See: https://businessyokohama.com/blog/2026/04/29/japangatewayforclimatetech/)
1.	Introduction 

2.	Keynote: “How NYC is Building the Next Climate Tech Hubs"
- Nicole Spina, Vice President, Climate Innovation & Industry Development, New York City Economic Development Corporation ((NYCEDC) 

3.	Fireside Chat: Where to Scale Next: US–Japan Investor Perspectives on Climate & Deep Tech

4.	Startup Pitch
Selected startups participating in the pitch session include companies working across fusion energy, circular materials, thermal electrification, critical mineral recovery, and advanced sensing technologies. Several are backed by leading investors, strategic industrial partners, and U.S. federal programs.
• Realta Fusion — Compact Fusion Energy
A university spinout developing modular magnetic mirror fusion systems for industrial-scale deployment. The company achieved a world-record 17 Tesla magnetic field on confined plasma and is backed by a $36M Series A and U.S. DOE fusion program support.
• Evrnu — Circular Textile Materials
Commercializing regenerative lyocell fiber made from post-consumer cotton waste, capable of being recycled multiple times without quality degradation. The company has secured over $330M in purchase commitments from global apparel brands.
• MIMiC Systems — Next-Generation Heat Pumps
Developing solid-state heat pumps with no refrigerants and no moving parts, targeting major reductions in HVAC energy consumption and emissions through advanced thermoelectric systems.
• FAST Metals — Critical Mineral Recovery
Recovering rare earths and high-value minerals from industrial waste streams through a proprietary low-energy hydrometallurgical process. The company is backed by a major global mining player.
• Florrent — Grid-Scale Energy Storage
Developing next-generation ultracapacitors for renewable integration, EV charging infrastructure, and grid stabilization. The company’s proprietary low-cost energy storage technology targets critical power stability gaps that conventional batteries cannot efficiently address.

5.	Networking

AI is radically changing how software is built. Tools can now generate prototypes in hours — sometimes minutes. But speed alone doesn’t create successful products.

​​​This side event explores the real difference between “vibe coding” — fast, AI-generated code driven by intuition — and AI-driven development with an expert in the loop, where AI accelerates delivery without sacrificing quality, security, or long-term value.

We’ll break down when rapid AI prototyping is good enough, when it becomes risky, and how founders, product leaders, and innovation teams can use AI responsibly to deliver MVPs that are not just fast — but fundable, scalable, and production-ready.

​​​What you’ll learn?

​​​Vibe Coding vs AI-Driven Development
Understand where AI-only coding works, where it fails, and why expert oversight is the difference between a demo and a real product.

​​​The hidden risks of fast AI-built MVPs
Learn why many AI-generated prototypes collapse under investor scrutiny due to poor architecture, security gaps, and technical debt.

​​​Expert-in-the-loop MVP delivery
See how experienced engineers and architects guide AI to ensure clean architecture, compliance, scalability, and knowledge retention.

​​​From idea to production roadmap
Get a practical blueprint for turning AI-assisted prototypes into systems that can survive real users, real traffic, and real growth.

​​​Who should attend?

​​​First-time startup founders
Learn why flashy demos rarely convince investors — and how to build an MVP that balances speed with credibility.

​​​Serial entrepreneurs
Discover how to reduce MVP cost and timelines without repeating mistakes that lead to fragile systems and lost ROI.

​​​Enterprises & innovation teams
Validate new product ideas quickly while keeping core engineering teams focused — and avoid creating future technical debt.

​​​Product & tech leaders
Understand how to integrate AI into your development process without losing control over quality, security, or strategy.

​​​Why attend?

​​​AI won’t replace engineering expertise — but teams that combine AI with the right experts will outperform those who rely on speed alone.

​​​This session is a practical, no-hype conversation about how modern teams build software responsibly in the age of AI — whether you’re launching your first startup or innovating inside a large organization.

partiful-vp9dwpmj5h3v8wv5k4g5.description:
​Leaders are regularly asked to make high-stakes decisions: where to invest, which interventions to prioritize, and how to allocate limited resources for the greatest impact. And these decisions only grow harder as systems become more deeply intertwined, consequences less predictable, and the stakes higher. Yet the tools we rely on weren't built for this. Large language models and conventional ML share a critical blind spot: they can't predict how a system will respond to an intervention it has never encountered before. To navigate today's complexity, we need tools that can reason beyond historical precedent and anticipate the downstream effects of the choices we make.

Anthos is a simulation platform that lets investors, philanthropies, and policymakers stress-test decisions before they commit capital or sign policy. It ingests the relevant literature, then applies neuro-symbolic causal inference to model the second- and third-order consequences spreadsheets and standard forecasting tend to miss. Non-technical users can run "what-if" scenarios through conversational AI and quickly see whether an investment thesis or policy proposal holds up under pressure.

Be among the first to experience Anthos. In this intimate, hands-on workshop, founders Devin Young (CEO) and DJ Passey (CTO) — joined by advisor C. Robin Castelli, MSc (former Global Head of Climate Modeling Analytics at Citi) and World Bank design partner Jasmin Sadegh — will run live model demonstrations. Then you'll have the chance to build your own causal models in Anthos, guided by our AI agents.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

AI can write the code now, but who's designing what it builds? Louise Macfadyen, author of the newly released O'Reilly book, Designing AI Interfaces, joins Bethany Crystal for a conversation that starts with a deceptively simple question: What does it mean to design AI-native systems and interfaces?

​Together they'll explore the philosophy and surprises of designing AI systems, poking at questions like: Who counts as a designer now? What does good taste looks like in a prompt-driven world? What happens when the coding is the easy part? Then they'll put it to the test.

Bethany and Louise will take a design concept from the book and build it live, in real time (using AI), showing what it looks like when design thinking drives the engineering, not the other way around. They'll close with a reflection on what worked, what surprised them, and what it means for anyone building with AI today.

​Key Takeaways:

- ​Understand the core principles of AI interface design from the author who literally wrote the book on it

- ​Watch design thinking applied live, from concept to working prototype in real time

​- Rethink your own role: You don't need to be a "designer" to start designing better AI experiences

​Target Audience:

- ​Product managers, designers, and builders working on AI-powered products who want a sharper design lens

- ​Founders and operators using AI tools daily who want to move from "it works" to "it works well" and understand why the difference matters

- ​Copies of the book, Designing AI Interfaces, will be available for purchase.

​—

​Co-hosts: Bethany Crystal (Founder & CEO, Build First - https://buildfirst.ai/) + Louise Macfadyen (Author, Designing AI Interfaces, O'Reilly Media)

​Hosted at Studio Rodrigo's design studio in DUMBO
​https://www.studiorodrigo.com/

Together with Justworks and leaders from companies including Snappy, NICE, Amdocs, Compete, and more, we’ll discuss how AI is reshaping hiring, people management, leadership, and organizational culture.


AI is no longer just another productivity tool, it’s changing how companies hire, manage teams, build culture, and scale.

Join us for an evening bringing together founders, operators, HR leaders, and executives to discuss what leadership looks like in the age of AI. From AI-first organizations and leaner teams to talent strategy, employee trust, and the future role of HR — this conversation is about the real operational changes already happening inside modern companies.

In collaboration with Justworks and Bereisheet Tech.

Agenda

5:30 PM — Networking & Drinks

6:30 PM — Panel Discussion:

AI-First Companies: How Founders Must Rethink Hiring, Management & Culture

AI is fundamentally changing how modern companies are built. Teams are becoming leaner, workflows faster, and expectations from employees and managers are evolving in real time.

This conversation will explore what it actually means to build an “AI-first” organization today — from hiring and productivity to culture, trust, and leadership. The panel will discuss how founders and executives should rethink organizational structures, what skills will matter most in the next few years, and where human leadership becomes even more important as automation expands.

We’ll also discuss practical realities:

How AI is already changing recruiting and talent evaluation

What happens to middle management in AI-driven organizations

Whether startups will hire fewer people — or simply different people

How to maintain culture and employee engagement during rapid transformation

The balance between operational efficiency and human connection

What founders are getting wrong about internal AI adoption

The session will include audience Q&A and open discussion with founders and operators in the room.

Moderator:

Noa Lotan, NICE

Noa Lotan is a senior HR leader at NiCE with more than 20 years of global HR experience across multinational organizations, including Comverse, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, and NiCE. specialises in talent strategy, organizational effectiveness and leadership development. partnering with executive leadership teams to drive workforce transformation and scalable people initiatives worldwide. Her work focuses on aligning business strategy with talent, leadership and the evolving impact of AI in HR.

Speakers:

Hamutal Oren-Fox, Snappy

Hamutal Oren-Fox is the Chief People Officer at Snappy, where she leads the People and Culture function, focusing on creating an environment where employees feel valued, engaged, and empowered. Before joining Snappy, Hamutal served as a Chief People Officer at Venn City and EVP of People at Cuebiq, where she played a key role in establishing the company’s HR function and thriving initiatives to enhance employee performance and engagement.

Amit Rapaport, Compete

Amit Rapaport is the Co-founder and CEO of Compete, an AI-powered workforce intelligence platform helping HR leaders make smarter, faster decisions with confidence. With over a decade of HR leadership experience at high-growth technology companies including SentinelOne and Palo Alto Networks, Amit founded Compete to transform fragmented people data into actionable insights for HR, Finance, and executive teams. Today, Compete helps organizations uncover workforce risks, identify opportunities, and modernize how they manage compensation, performance, and strategic workforce planning in the age of AI.

Leadership from Justworks


7:00 PM — Fireside Chat:

Building and Leading Teams in the AI Era

Beyond the headlines and tools, AI is forcing leaders to rethink how they personally manage, communicate, prioritize, and execute inside their organizations.

In this fireside chat, we’ll move from theory to real operator experiences: how leadership changes when teams move faster, expectations increase, and employees themselves are adapting to entirely new ways of working.

The conversation will touch on:

How leadership styles are evolving in AI-driven companies

The changing expectations from employees and managers

Decision-making in a world of constant AI acceleration

Managing uncertainty, fear, and resistance internally

How operators personally use AI in their day-to-day work

What remains uniquely human in leadership

What the future workplace may realistically look like in 3–5 years

This will be an open and candid discussion designed for founders, executives, and leaders navigating these changes in real time.


Fireside Chat:

Idit Duvdevany Aronsohn, Amdocs

Idit Duvdevany-Aronsohn heads ESG and People Relations at Amdocs – a global telecommunications software & services company [NASDAQ:DOX] with over 26,000 employees worldwide. In this role, Idit focuses on improving the lives of people in our communities, fostering diversity & inclusion, promoting sustainability with technologies, prioritizing workplace practices & employee wellbeing. Her responsibilities include ensuring that Amdocs’ global ESG, employment strategies, and global people relations create lasting value.



7:30 PM — Networking



About the Organizers

Justworks￼

Justworks is a technology company that levels the playing field for all small businesses. Through our software and as a partner, we help our customers take care of their teams, streamline their operations, and navigate the complex aspects of managing a workforce with confidence.

Bereisheet Tech￼

Bereisheet Tech is the leading Israeli high-tech community on the U.S. East Coast, connecting founders, executives, investors, and operators through curated events and professional communities.

What would you say about AI right now if no one could trace it back to you?

TRUE CONFESSIONS is a candid, facilitated conversation about the AI boom's real impact on fundraising.  We'll cut through the hype so founders and investors can make better decisions based on what's actually happening.

Hosted by Flywheel Strategy x Tech/ish during NY Tech Week, this session brings together investors, AI founders, and non-AI founders for a structured discussion grounded in anonymous feedback and sentiment from those in the room and outside experts.

The Problem

AI hype is distorting capital markets — pressuring AI companies to overstate, making non-AI founders feel locked out, and skewing perception for everyone keeping up through headlines.

How It Works

Attendees complete an anonymous pre-event survey where unpopular opinions are welcome. We open by sharing what the room actually believes: where investors feel pressure to deploy, where AI founders feel pressure to overstate, where non-AI founders feel locked out. Then we dig in.
No panels. No pitching. No performative takes.

You'll Leave With

- Clarity on signal vs. hype: a grounded read on what’s actually driving AI fundraising decisions right now (and what’s just noise)
- Unfiltered market insight:  real, anonymous sentiment from founders and investors you won’t hear on stage or in press cycles
- Actionable positioning edge: how to navigate (or leverage) the AI narrative whether you’re building in AI or not, to raise and compete more effectively

AI agents that use computers like humans are here. What does that mean for how we work and live? We’re fortunate to have one of the world’s leading AI innovators — Ang Li, PhD — joining us for this exclusive evening. Ang is the CEO and co-founder of Simular, the autonomous computer company, and his work spans the frontier of artificial intelligence: autonomous driving, lifelong autonomous agents, video intelligence, computer vision, mapping systems, and AI-powered advertising.

Over his career, Ang has held research and engineering roles at some of the most influential AI organizations in the world — Google DeepMind, Baidu Apollo, Facebook AI Research, the Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute, Apple, Google Street View, and Comcast Labs DC. He holds a PhD in Computer Science, with research focused on spatial perception through visual and linguistic information — pioneering work at the intersection of AI, robotics, and human-machine understanding.

At Simular, that research has become product. Simular’s agent was the first in the world to surpass human-level performance on OSWorld ￼, the leading benchmark for AI that operates real computers — and the company is backed by $21.5M led by Felicis, with participation from NVIDIA’s NVentures and Basis Set Ventures ￼.

And you’ll see it live. Watch Sai (https://sai.work/) — one of the world’s most advanced AI assistants — do real work on a real computer, right in front of you. Unlike chatbots that just hand you answers, Sai operates your computer: browsing the web, filling out forms, creating files, sending emails, and completing multi-step tasks from start to finish. It’s like having an executive assistant who never sleeps, never forgets, and works at the speed of light.

No slides. No buzzwords. Just AI doing actual work.

A 30-Minute Panel + Networking at Tavern Community Coworking.
As a founder, you're constantly deciding what to do yourself, what to hire for, and what to buy or build a tool for. But AI is changing that equation—fast.
Entire categories of work that used to require a hire, an agency, or a vendor can now be handled by AI tools. At the same time, the need for human judgment is getting higher, not lower. There’s a critical difference between outsourcing a task and outsourcing judgment. 
The risk isn’t just delegating work—it’s losing control of decisions that define your company. Get it wrong and you're either burning cash or burning out. 
This panel is about getting it right.
We'll dig into how to figure out which parts of your business need you, which are better handed off to an external specialist, and which problems already have a tech solution waiting for you. This discussion will help you move faster without losing control of the things that actually matter.
We're bringing together founders who've been in the weeds, operators who've built the systems, vendors who sell the solutions, and investors who've watched it play out to give you insights from experience you can use for your own discernment.  
After the panel, stick around for bagels and Coffee and to connect with fellow founders, potential partners and investors.

🚀 Successful exits: what founders should be doing now to get there.

Most early-stage founders focus on product, growth, and fundraising. The companies that consistently outperform are doing something else early, they're building the right people around them and structuring those relationships to actually drive outcomes. 

Join us for a high-impact morning designed for pre-seed to Series B founders who want to build smarter, scale faster, and unlock access to capital.

We will demystify advisory and governing boards and show you how they can accelerate growth, strengthen your investor narrative, and open doors to capital. We'll start with a short fireside on exits; what founders get wrong, how early decisions shape outcomes, and why the people around you matter more than most realize. Then we'll zoom out to the full playbook.

Advisory boards, governing boards, strategic advisors - these are the most underleveraged tools in a founder's arsenal, and experienced entrepreneurs never leave this value on the table.

Why? How to actually build, structure, compensate, and paper these relationships has been nearly impossible to find in one place. Until now.

🎓 You'll walk away knowing:
- the difference between advisory and governing boards and when to build each
- how the right board increases your fundability and investor confidence, practical strategies for structuring, compensating, and managing boards early
- how to identify and recruit high-impact members — and why diversity on your board leads to stronger decisions and better outcomes

💡 Boards should not be scary. They should be your rocket fuel.

Real-world lessons, common pitfalls, actionable frameworks. You'll hear from a VC, an M&A lawyer, and an operator-turned-founder on what the best companies do differently. Whether you're pre-seed or preparing for your next round, you'll leave with the clarity and tools to turn your board into a true strategic advantage, not the other way around.

Your spot is NOT confirmed until payment is received via the Venmo link below. Unpaid RSVPs will be moved to the waitlist to open up spots for active founders.

In a sea of complex scientific, medical, and technical claims, the investor's brain is naturally skeptical. The ultimate differentiator isn’t your IP; it's how you pitch it. You must translate deep science into high-stakes commercial potential without losing scientific accuracy.

In this intensive 90-minute pitch clinic, neuroscience-based executive communication coach Jennifer Pawlitschek teaches you how to cut through the clinical data, build immediate neural authority, and anchor your scientific value proposition in the minds of high-stakes investors.

🚀 Kick Off Tech Week with Authority
Held on the first week of NY Tech Week prep, this clinic ensures you stand out when competition is at its peak. Master your narrative so you can pitch with total conviction at every mixer, panel, and demo day.

Key Takeaways:

The Pre-Clinic Neuro-Audit: Submit your slides ahead of time. Jennifer will personally review your deck beforehand to identify exactly where dense scientific data and clinical slides are losing the investor's brain.

The 60-Second Hook: Polish your opening minute to translate complex science into immediate commercial potential and capture the room.

Neuro-Presence & Delivery: Align your physical, vocal, and non-verbal cues to project executive presence, handle academic presentation habits, and trigger immediate investor trust.

Q&A Defense: Master the psychological frameworks needed to answer complex technical, clinical, and regulatory objections with absolute conviction.

What Other Founders Say:

"Jennifer helped us translate our complex clinical trial data into a commercial story VCs actually wanted to fund. She showed us how to respect the science while pitching the business."
— Dr. A.B., Co-Founder of Stealth Therapeutics Startup

"We used to lose investors by slide three with deep biochemistry jargon. Jennifer's Neuro-Audit completely streamlined our narrative. The difference in investor engagement was night and day."
— H.M., CEO of Gene Editing Platform

"Nailing the first 60 seconds was our biggest challenge as scientific founders. Jennifer's presence coaching gave me the physical and vocal authority to command the room instantly."

New model drops. New framework. New "this changes everything" thread. By the time you've integrated one tool, three more have made it obsolete.

So we asked ourselves a different question: what doesn't change? Across enterprise teams, across codebases, across the hype cycles. Which engineering practices actually hold up when the underlying models rotate every quarter?

Artur Skowroński and Tomasz Lelek spent a year shipping AI-assisted code across enterprise clients, watching what broke and what survived, then committed the patterns to print in Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs, co-published with Manning Publications.

Join Artur and Tomasz for a discussion panel and community mixer, and learn about:
- Where AI earns its place in the delivery cycle, and where it creates new debt 
- Vibe coding beyond the individual contributor: what changes at team and org scale
- Keeping quality and trust intact when half your code has a co-author 
- Staying fast without losing control of what ships

And if you are interested in writing a book yourself, Artur and Tomasz will also talk about:
- Picking the right topic, so that the trend is still relevant when the book is out
- Getting past the writer’s block
- What reputable publishers like Manning are actually looking for right now

After the panel, you are invited over for drinks, networking, and the kind of conversations that don't happen in Slack.

Bonus: We'll be giving away 30 demo copies of Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs. Grab one and get it signed by Artur and Tomasz in person.

partiful-ssoqr8v1u9os3khp517r.description:
AI agents are moving from demos to production. They execute payments, write code, access sensitive data, and ship decisions to clients without a human in the loop. 

The safety infrastructure has not kept up, and this workshop is focused on fixing that.

Today's guardrails are assertions, not proofs. They only work most of the time, fail silently in the cases that matter, and can be hijacked by a single line of injected text. Every public agent incident ends with the same question: how do you prove the agent followed the rule?

We'll learn how missing layer is cryptographic guarantees, not better prompts or more filters: mathematical proof that an agent action complies with your policy before it runs.  

This workshop teaches you how to easily build formal verification of agent policy before each action; defenses that survive prompt injection; and portable receipts your security team, counterparty and your auditor can easily verify. 

Hands-on and accessible to all - we hope to see you there!

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

Tech Week can be chaotic. Running between panels, pitching, networking, and feeling overstimulated. The Oasis is a daily retreat: a place to belong, breathe, and actually co-create.

We're building a persistent home base across the week where builders, founders, and creatives show up every day to flow together, have real conversations around meaningful topics, and leave refreshed and inspired. The series blends daily 'co-flow' drop-in sessions with curated collaborative programming: roundtable discussions, fireside chats, and mentor office hours. Each day seeds Flowstate Sparks, structured artifacts that keep the conversation going long after the week ends.

Day 2: The Future of Work

Today we sit with one of the most consequential questions of this moment: what happens to work as AI and automation accelerate? If technology continues to absorb the things we used to do for a paycheck, what gets freed up, and what do we choose to do with it? We'll explore the shift from working out of need to creating out of passion, the new shapes careers and companies might take, and what it means to build a life that holds up when the old scripts no longer apply. Expect honest conversation about both the opportunity and the uncertainty.

With thanks to our venue partner, BELONG NYC

The Oasis is hosted at BELONG NYC (@belong.nyc), a hospitality-driven workspace and urban sanctuary in the heart of SoHo. Think airport lounge meets coworking: a high-design, high-service environment purpose-built for the in-between moments of life in motion. Beyond hosting our series, BELONG offers Flowstate members on-demand access to private meeting rooms, phone booths, and hot desks, plus showers and changing facilities, secure luggage storage, and rentable lockers throughout Tech Week. If you're juggling flights, workouts, dinners, and back-to-back meetings, it's the place to reset and keep going.

For decades, the systems that underpin work — benefits, healthcare, and financial stability — were built around a single assumption: one job, one employer, one steady income.

That assumption is breaking.

Today, millions of Americans earn across multiple roles, platforms, and income streams — a structural shift often referred to as the "microshifting workforce." But the systems designed to support them haven't kept up.

As this shift accelerates, the gaps are becoming harder to ignore: lost coverage, fragmented care, and systems that weren't designed for movement.

At the same time, new technologies, particularly AI, are beginning to reshape how individuals navigate fragmented systems, manage care, and coordinate across multiple sources of income.

Join us for a conversation with leaders Ellyn Shook, former CHRO of Accenture; Susan Podlogar, former CHRO of MetLife; and Tim Massa, EVP and CHRO of Kroger. Moderated by Bradley Tusk, founder and CEO of Tusk Ventures, with Felix W. Ortiz III, founder and CEO of Smirk Health.

This panel brings together leaders across tech, healthcare, and the future of work to explore what happens when foundational systems fall out of sync—and what's being built to replace them.

partiful-dzxbz2nm6cjxkgeabimd.description:
Join Norton Rose Fulbright during New York Tech Week for an intimate happy hour at the intersection of innovation, intellectual property and artificial intelligence.

As AI reshapes how companies create, compete and commercialize, a strong IP strategy is no longer just about protection. It's about turning your intellectual assets into meaningful revenue while navigating an increasingly complex legal landscape. This evening will explore how founders, technologists and legal leaders can move beyond defensive IP strategies to actively monetize innovation in the AI age, without stepping on the rights of others.

Partner Johanna Schmitt and Counsel Sam Eichner from Norton Rose Fulbright's Brands Group, along with Stephanie DeBrow from the firm's Patent Disputes practice, will kick off the evening with a brief presentation covering timely topics, including:

Monetizing your IP
•	Copyright in the age of AI: Who owns AI-generated content? How are courts and regulators approaching authorship, fair use and training data liability?
•	Trademark strategy for AI-driven brands: Protecting and monetizing brand identity in a world of AI-generated names, logos and marketing assets
•	Patent monetization: Structuring licensing programs, identifying monetization opportunities and navigating patent disputes in emerging tech
•	Building a holistic IP portfolio: Integrating patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets into a coordinated commercial strategy
•	Licensing and commercialization: How companies can structure IP licensing deals to generate revenue and strategic advantage in AI-driven markets

Avoiding infringement: What tech businesses need to know
•	Copyright clearance & AI training data: Understanding the risks of using third-party content to train AI models and how to implement responsible data sourcing practices
•	Trademark clearance and brand adoption: Why conducting thorough clearance searches before launching a new brand, product name or logo is essential, and what the consequences of skipping this step can be
•	Patent freedom to operate: How to assess whether a new product or technology infringes existing patents before going to market, and strategies for mitigating exposure
•	Open source compliance: The often overlooked IP obligations that come with incorporating open source software into commercial products
•	Third-party content and  licensing: Best practices for securing rights to images, music, text and software to avoid unintentional infringement across your platforms and products

HardTech Forum hosted by MistyWest (www.mistywest.com) and presented by Intent (https://www.withintent.com/)

---

Since Kevin Ashton coined "Internet of Things" in 1999, the promise of real-time tracking has finally become practical, built on RFID, BLE, cellular telematics, and satellite connectivity. Devices now run 10 years on a single battery, and new systems are experimenting with Bluetooth signals detected directly by satellites.

After our April 9th Vancouver HardTech Forum on The Internet of Moving Things, MistyWest and Intent are bringing the conversation to NYC with The Internet of Building Things. Construction is one of the hardest environments to digitize—chaotic, temporary, and GPS-denied—but autonomous drones, LiDAR, and adapted fleet sensor stacks are changing that fast. This HardTech Forum asks: now that we can see the physical world with unprecedented resolution, where does the real value get created, in the hardware, the data, or the platforms that turn sensor feeds into decisions?

---
SPEAKERS

Ben Williams - COO at Exyn Technologies (www.exyn.com/)

Ben is the COO/CPO of Exyn Technologies, pioneering GPS-denied autonomy in multi-modal robots. Previously, he co-founded and led Reelio (acquired by Fullscreen Media/AT&T), helped commercialize deep tech at Lockheed Martin, and earned his MBA from Wharton — where he was later named to their 40 Under 40. A former US Naval Officer and recovering engineer, he also mentors early-stage startups and serves on various boards, all while keeping his two young sons out of the snack cabinet.

Niran Shrestha - CEO at Kwant.ai

Niran Shrestha is the CEO of Kwant.ai, an AI-powered industrial workforce management platform using wearable technology to improve safety, productivity, and compliance on job sites. Deployed by ENR 500 contractors like Kiewit, Turner, and Walbridge, and Fortune 200 companies including Ford, Microsoft, and General Motors, Kwant's flagship projects include Ford's Blue Oval City (24K workers), major Microsoft data centers, and Nucor's largest steel plant — with case studies showing a 50% reduction in safety incidents and an 11% productivity gain.

Conley Oster - COO & Co-Founder at Raise Robotics (www.raiserobotics.ai/)

Conley is COO and Co-Founder of Raise Robotics, deploying mobile robotic systems across construction, shipbuilding, and heavy industry to automate high-risk, labor-intensive field work. He leads commercialization, partnerships, and deployment strategy — and brings a grounded perspective from a career in construction equipment, field operations, and heavy industrial sales that informs how Raise bridges the gap from promising technology to scalable adoption on real jobsites.
---

​The HardTech Forum (https://mistywest.com/hardtech-forum) series would not be possible without gold sponsors Intent, and silver sponsors Nordic Semiconductor, and Boast. We extend to them endless thanks for enabling us to host such incredible events!

Intent (https://withintent.com/) is a Polish software design and engineering firm specializing in connected devices, with clients like Oura, Bose, and Nike.

Nordic (https://nordicsemi.com/) makes the wireless chips powering the world's most advanced connected devices.

Boast (https://boast.ai/) is a Vancouver-based platform that automates SR&ED and R&D tax credit claims, helping North American hardware and deep tech companies recover up to 64% of eligible R&D expenses with less paperwork and audit risk.

When adopting customer-facing AI, companies often start with service. But now, the most forward-thinking teams are taking a more holistic approach. They're not just using an AI Agent for service – they're collapsing the walls between support, success, and sales, to build a more a connected customer experience.

For Clay, the transformation is already underway. They've embedded GTM engineering into Ops teams to drive support efficiency at scale. Support Engineering is placed at the intersection of CX teams to reduce volume by fixing issues and building internal tools. Support and Success are becoming more collaborative— moving from focusing volume management to building durable customer relationships.

Fin is building toward the same future — a single Customer Agent that delivers a seamless customer experience — from sales to service to success.

Join Declan Ivory, VP of Customer Support at Fin / Intercom, and George Dilthey, Head of Support at Clay, for an honest conversation about what scaling CX with AI actually looks like in practice — the org changes, the use cases you haven't tried yet, and where this is all heading.

This one's for teams who are past the starting line and ready to talk about what comes next.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

Human judgment in an age of intelligent systems

Hosted by Mothers to Daughters (M2D), a global platform advancing intergenerational mentorship and economic empowerment, this conversation reflects a broader mission:

This session brings that philosophy into practice, offering a space where capital, technology, and human judgment converge, and where proximity leads to possibility.

This is not a traditional panel. It’s a high-signal room designed for thoughtful exchange, meaningful connections, and a deeper look into how decisions are actually made.

partiful-e2hnod2jizhnhqujwmqu.description:
AI is not just a technological shift - it’s a restructuring of the labor market.

White-collar roles are compressing. Entry-level pathways are breaking. Entire categories of work are being reorganized faster than new ones are being created.

At the same time, demand is rising for real, task-based capability - often in areas the market has historically overlooked or misunderstood.

We’re entering a moment where:
> Output is becoming abundant
> But signal on human capability is increasingly scarce

This salon brings together a curated group of founders, investors, and operators to explore how labor markets are evolving - and where capital is likely to flow next.

We’ll discuss:
> Where displaced talent goes - and where new demand is actually emerging
> What replaces traditional entry pathways - and who controls access to opportunity
> Which sectors expand vs. contract - and why the market may be mispricing both
> Where talent is being undervalued - and how that creates asymmetric opportunity
> What new infrastructure is needed - and which companies could define it

Join Light Dao, and conscious investors and entrepreneurs for an evening filled with connection and deep conversations with Jenny Fielding, Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Everywhere Ventures, and Shrinidhi Rao, Director of Workforce Innovation at The Burning Glass Institute.

Guest Speaker: Jenny Fielding
Jenny Fielding is one of the most active global pre-seed investors, having been the first money into 300+ startups across a portfolio worth over $10B. As Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Everywhere Ventures, she leads a thriving community of 500+ founders and operators investing across money, health, and work. Formerly Managing Director at Techstars, Jenny is a 2x founder, lawyer by training, and an Adjunct Professor at Columbia University and Cornell Tech. Her forthcoming book, Venture Everywhere, distills her global perspective on building purpose-driven companies. More info: https://www.jennyfielding.com/venture-everywhere

Guest Speaker: Shrinidhi Rao
Shrinidhi Rao is Director of Workforce Innovation at The Burning Glass Institute - a leading research organization focused on the future of work, skills-based hiring, and labor market transformation. His work sits at the intersection of workforce strategy, labor market intelligence, and economic mobility, helping organizations understand how AI, shifting workforce demands, and evolving hiring systems are reshaping opportunity and talent allocation across industries.

​The interactive wildfire workshop simulates real-world wildfire challenges with game-based learning. In the workshop, participants will collaborate and make resilience investment decisions to explore ways to mitigate and adapt to the growing wildfire risks.

​In most cases, investment will be easy if we have unlimited resources and complete information. Unfortunately, most of our decisions will have trade-offs and complex uncertainties.

​If we would love to mitigate the wildfire damages, what are the decision blind spots we should consider? And what are the climate actions we should first prioritize?

​Join our workshop and shape our future with wildfire-resilience practices.

​

​Recommended Audience

​Aspiring Climate Fellows: Advance the knowledge for wildfire mitigation and adaptation

​Social Climate Influencers: Promote wildfire knowledge and action to local communities.

​Corporate Investment: Revisit the location vulnerability with mitigation and adaptation investment.

​The workshop's main value will come from discussion and reflection. No climate background is required—just curiosity to explore more with others.

​

​Expected Outcomes

​✅ Understand the complexity and the trade-off for wildfire prevention

​✅ Explore wildfire resilience investment strategy with various actions

​✅ Strengthen cross-sector collaboration with workshop stakeholders

​Trauma-Informed Practices

​If you and/or your family members or friends have recently experienced a wildfire, please kindly self-evaluate your current condition for participation. During the workshop, if you feel uncomfortable, please notify the speaker and stop the engagement. If needed, we recommend seeking professional support.

​

​As a climate stakeholder, if you would love to solve multiple climate problems, at scale, in time, with limited resources, at a highest possible success rate…

Your AI prototype works on your laptop. Now what?

Most non-technical founders hit a wall when their demo needs to become a real product. Auth, costs, latency, observability, evals, deploys, rollback. The things engineers take for granted are the things that scare you most.

In this 90-minute working session, we'll take a small group of non-technical founders through the same checklist Tequity uses to ship our clients' products from prototype to production:

- Audit what's actually production-blocking vs. what feels scary but isn't
- Map your real costs at 100, 1,000, and 10,000 users
- Identify the 5 things that will break first when you launch
- Write a one-page production readiness brief you can hand to a dev team (or use to hire one)

This is hands-on. Bring your prototype (or a screenshot of it). You'll leave with a checklist you can act on this week.

- Non-technical founders who have a working prototype and don't know what "production" actually requires
- Founders who built something with Claude, Cursor, Lovable, or Bolt and are stuck on what comes next
- Anyone who's been told "you can't ship that" but doesn't know which parts are real

Build your team for the AI Era: A working session for founders and operators

Not a panel. Not a presentation. A hands-on session where you leave with something real.

Most teams are letting people go, handing work to agents, and then realizing no one knows how to manage, debug, or course-correct when things break. The org chart isn't just a people problem anymore and most teams have no framework for thinking about it.

What we'll do:

Part 1: Design Getting everyone on the same page, literally. We'll start with a shared vocabulary (what is an AI agent vs. AI, what is an AI Orchestrator, where do agents sit in a reporting structure) and then work through how to reimagine an org chart with both human and agent roles mapped explicitly. Where does discretion live? Where does transactional work get handed off? Who owns the system when it breaks?

Part 2: Implementation Once the design is clear, the harder question: how do you actually build toward it? This is where workflow architecture, change management, and the culture of how humans and agents operate together come into focus.

What you'll walk away with:

1) A reimagined version of your org structure and new roles identified, handoffs mapped. 
2) A "Before & After" org chart visualization showing where agents plug in and where humans move up to Orchestrator. 
3) An AI usage diagnostic: where you are vs. where you could be

***Bring your laptop to be able to participate in the session.

Why Britt & Mina: Britt has spent four years deploying fractional operators onto early and growth-stage teams, a model that's essentially a preview of where all teams are heading. Mina brings the AI implementation layer, including a sharp framework for thinking about agents the way we once thought about org hierarchy. Together: here's how to design it, and here's how to build it.

partiful-ya9fboo26bt6i1n8ha72.description:
In partnership with the Healthcare Club of NY and Caseflow AI (usecaseflow.ai) for NY TECH WEEK.

New York is about to decide something the rest of the country will be watching: whether chatbot companies should be on the hook when their AI gives medical, legal, or mental health advice that causes harm.

Senate Bill S7263, sponsored by State Senator Kristen Gonzalez, would make chatbot operators civilly liable when their AI provides "substantive" advice in domains covered by professional licensing law. That's 14+ licensed professions plus the practice of law. Disclaimers don't save you. A "you're talking to a bot" notice doesn't save you. And the private right of action means anyone harmed can sue.

Supporters say it's common sense: if a human pretending to be a doctor can be prosecuted, a chatbot that hallucinates a medical license shouldn't get a free pass. Critics say the bill is vague about what counts as "substantive" advice, puts nonprofit and government chatbots in the same legal crosshairs as OpenAI, and ends up taxing the people who most need low-cost information (tenants, patients, small business owners) on behalf of licensed incumbents who don't love the competition.
Both sides have a point. That's why we're putting them in a room.

Against S7263:
Sateesh Nori: attorney, legal tech founder (LawDroid), and one of the more thoughtful voices arguing that restricting AI legal guidance hurts the people the legal system already fails.

For S7263:
Dr. Cecilia Dones: data and analytics practitioner-academic, founder of 3 Standard Deviations, and a faculty member at Columbia's School of Professional Studies. Her work sits at the intersection of AI, data, and trust: translating what these systems actually do for organizations, consumers, and the people who get caught in between.

💡 What’s the Ugly Truth
People are not going to shop the way they do now forever. The shift is already starting. Consumers will increasingly ask AI agents to search, compare, recommend, and in some cases buy for them.
That means brands cannot rely on the old playbook alone. If discovery moves from browsers and marketplaces to AI-led interfaces, brands risk losing attention, pricing power, customer data, and margin.
The real question is not whether agentic commerce is coming. It is whether your brand will know how to compete when the buyer is no longer a person clicking through your storefront, but an AI making the shortlist.

🎯 Why You Should Attend
-Learn what agentic commerce actually looks like right now, not just the hype.
-Understand how shopping behavior may shift over the next 5 to 10 years.
-Get clear on what parts of the old ecommerce playbook still matter, and what is starting to break.
-Learn where brands should invest now to stay discoverable, defensible, and profitable.
-Avoid expensive mistakes around channels, data, pricing, and customer acquisition.
-Meet the founders, operators, and researchers shaping this shift in real time.

🙋 Who's Getting In This Room
-Brand owners
-Ecommerce tech founders
-Retailers
-Growth and marketing leaders
-Researchers studying consumer behavior and digital commerce
-Builders working on AI shopping, search, recommendation, and agent infrastructure
-Investors focused on AI and digital commerce

🎤 Who’s Taking the Stage
Ali Mirzaei - Founder & CEO of Dimension Studios

Ali Mirzaei is the founder and CEO of Dimension Studios, the social commerce company behind Seller OS, an agentic AI platform that replaces TikTok's native Seller Center with a unified operational command center for brands and agencies. Ali built the #1 shop on TikTok within six months of the platform's US launch, and Dimension has since operated four #1 shops for clients including Liquid Death, Final Boss Sour, T3 Micro, SquidHaus, Bones Coffee, and more. The company is profitable at roughly $2.5M ARR with multiple product launches planned for 2026.


Joshua Cohen - Co-Founder & CEO of Pinpoint

Joshua Cohen is the founder of Pinpoint, the AI layer between social and revenue. Used by brands like Cozy Earth, Gopuff, Represent Clothing, and hundreds of others.

Moderator: 
Alan Zong - Co-Founder & Partner at UpScaleX

Alan Zong is Co-Founder and Partner at UpScaleX, a San Francisco-based seed fund investing in AI-native applications and commercial innovations. He brings 10+ years of experience across VC and CVC and has been an early backer of multiple unicorns and decacorns. Alan holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and previously led innovation investment at Alibaba International.

💬 What We Do Not Sugarcoat
-Brand loyalty may get weaker when AI optimizes for convenience, price, and speed.
-Paid media may become less effective if discovery shifts upstream into AI interfaces.
-Consumer behavior is changing faster than most brands are planning for.
-Brands may lose access to the clickstream signals that used to reveal intent, hesitation, and purchase readiness.
-Marketplaces and retailers may lose power if agents can bypass them and go more directly to sellers or alternative paths.
-Margin pressure gets worse if AI agents consistently surface the lowest-priced option.
If your brand is invisible to AI systems, it may become invisible to future buyers.
-A direct conversation for people trying to understand what happens when commerce stops being click-first and starts becoming agent-first.

📋 What Attendees Will Walk Away With
By the end of the session, attendees should leave with a clearer understanding of:
-How agentic commerce is beginning to show up in the market already
which risks and opportunities matter most for brands and commerce platforms
-Where to invest attention now, before the shift becomes obvious to everyone
-How to think about defensibility in a world where AI increasingly mediates buyer behavior
-Who else in the room may be worth building with, learning from, or partnering with 

🤝 Who's Backing This
UpScaleX - A Palo Alto–based seed fund and founders’ community investing in AI-native businesses and supporting the builders redefining how commerce is discovered, operated, and scaled.

Adelphi University - Your place. Your people. Your future. Accepted students, secure your spot today.

Last week, we tried breaking into 30 startups.

20 of them had severe vulnerabilities.

AI is writing code faster than ever - and nobody is securing it. Founders are shipping new features, instead of building a digital fortress. 

The result? 

A generation of products that look polished on the surface and are wide open underneath.

This isn't a theory talk. We're doing live hacks.

Bring your laptop. Bring your ego. Leave with a clearer picture of where your product actually stands.

What to expect:
- How hackers are approaching AI-generated codebases differently
- The most common (and embarrassing) vulnerabilities we keep finding
- Live breakins - on volunteer products in the room, and public startups
- What a real security baseline looks like for a startup that's already shipped

Who this is for:
Founders - technical or not - who have a live product and genuinely don't know if it's secure. Especially if you've leaned heavily on AI to build it.

What this is not:
A vendor pitch. 
A beginner's intro to cybersecurity. 
A safe space for your tech team.

partiful-l38ujelxqvhmfb60e3ka.description:
The New Math: How VC and PE Are Rethinking Capital in Women's Health

Presented during New York Tech Week

Women's health is having a moment—but the capital backing it remains uneven. Investors are paying unprecedented attention to the category, driven by its scale, its underserved patient base, and a wave of clinical and commercial validation. Yet beneath the surface, the financing landscape is anything but straightforward. Capital remains concentrated in a small number of high-profile deals, early- and growth-stage companies face persistent cliffs, and founders often find themselves navigating a mismatch between the businesses they're building and the investment models available to them.

Meanwhile, the investors themselves are evolving. Venture capital is recalibrating its timelines, its risk tolerance, and its assumptions about what constitutes a durable women's health business. Private equity is playing an increasingly central role, building platforms and infrastructure with a fundamentally different approach to value creation and scale. These two worlds—once distinct—are beginning to converge in ways that could redefine how women's health companies are financed, operated, and brought to market. The question is no longer whether this sector matters. It's what kind of capital will shape its next chapter.

This panel brings together venture and private equity investors active in or adjacent to women's health to explore:

👉🏼 Where the capital is really going—and where it isn't

👉🏼 How investors assess opportunity across stages, sectors, and business models

👉🏼 The trade-offs between speed, scale, and sustainability in today's approaches

👉🏼 Whether hybrid VC/PE models are emerging—and how founders should prepare

👉🏼 What the current dynamics mean for the next generation of women's health companies

This is a candid, strategic conversation for investors, founders, and ecosystem builders who want a clear-eyed view of where women's health investing stands today—and where it's headed next.

🔅 Who Should Attend: Investors across venture, growth equity, and private equity; founders and operators in women's health and healthcare services; limited partners with healthcare mandates; and ecosystem builders interested in the intersection of capital strategy and care delivery.

As robotics and automation accelerate across industries, most conversations remain abstract and focused on technology capabilities rather than real world deployment. 

Robotics adoption in U.S. manufacturing is accelerating. Nearly 400,000 industrial robots are now operating in U.S. factories, with tens of thousands added each year. At the same time, manufacturing continues to face a labor gap measured in the hundreds of thousands of open roles, with millions more projected this decade. But adoption is not the same as success. Most automation challenges do not fail at the level of technology. They fail on the factory floor, where people, process, training, safety, and operating constraints
determine whether systems work or stall.

Humans + Robots & The Factory Floor brings together operators, robotics companies, and systems leaders to explore what happens when automation meets the real world of production.

This session moves to examine the lived experience of integrating robotics into active manufacturing environments.

Why This Matters Now
Robotics adoption is increasing, but deployment challenges remain widespread. Many automation efforts fail not because of the technology itself, but because of misalignment with human systems.

Workforce, training, and operational realities are too often excluded from innovation conversations.

There is a growing need to connect startups, manufacturers, and workforce leaders in a shared dialogue.

This event addresses a critical gap by focusing on the intersection of technology an

New York Robotics (NYR) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the robotics and embodied AI industry across the regional, national, and global landscape — becoming a driving force for innovation, investment, and industry growth, positioning New York as a premier global hub for robotics

The American Manufacturing Futures Institute (AMFI) is a national 501(c)(3) advancing U.S. manufacturing through the intersection of policy, people, and place.

partiful-e8nhjnhwghmetllrfvq7.description:
What does it actually take to get people to trust something new with the things they care about? The founders on this panel have answered that question twice, ten years apart.

They built Venmo, Stripe, and the consumer fintech rails that now feel obvious. Getting people to send money through an app was a fight. Now they're in a different one: convincing engineers to share how they prompt, and convincing everyone else to trust a cloud computer with their files, their work, and their ideas.

Same trust barrier. Different decade. Same people figuring it out.

We're getting into the pattern match between early consumer fintech and where AI is right now (what's the same, what's actually new), the shift from mobile-first to AI-first and what that means for how you build, hire, and sell, when to take an exit vs. keep building, and how tribal knowledge inside a team turns from advantage into bottleneck. 

We'll close rapid-fire: best advice you ignored, advice you're ignoring right now.

Bring questions. Leave with quotes.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

partiful-048kyo6hrsdlwmwlmutm.description:
Agent memory is a mess. 

Most teams are stitching together a vector store, a graph database, and some middleware - three systems to manage, three potential failure points, and no guarantees any of it stays consistent. It works until it doesn't.

This meetup is about solving it properly. Not a quick fix, not another abstraction layer - memory that's transactional, structured, and built into the database itself. We'll show what that looks like in practice with Spectron, SurrealDB's brand new agent memory system.

We'll be joined by engineering teams from Pydantic and Tavily - covering how to structure and validate the data your agents work with, and how to handle retrieval at runtime without losing the plot mid-task.

Hard questions welcome. Drinks on us.
partiful-048kyo6hrsdlwmwlmutm.ogTitle: Agents in Production: The Memory Problem - #NYTechWeek | Partiful

As AI enters its next phase—from copilots to autonomous systems—the convergence of Robotics (Embodied AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) is reshaping how work gets done in the physical and digital world.

In this new paradigm, capital is not just funding software—it is underwriting end-to-end intelligent systems that integrate perception, reasoning, and action. From industrial automation and service robotics to agentic workflows and real-world deployment, a new category is emerging:
👉 “Service-as-Software” powered by Robotics + LLMs

This private roundtable convenes leading LPs, GPs, family offices, and frontier founders to explore how global capital can align with this shift—and where the most asymmetric opportunities lie.

1️⃣ Capital Flows into Robotics & Embodied AI
Where is smart money moving? From hardware-enabled AI to full-stack robotics platforms, we examine capital allocation strategies across the stack.

How LLMs are evolving from copilots to decision-making engines—powering robotics, automation, and real-world workflows.

Artificial Intelligence is moving beyond the digital world and into the physical one. This shift, often referred to as Physical AI, is quickly becoming one of the most important frontiers in the field.

Leading AI labs, global technology companies, and a new generation of startups are building the foundations for this transition. But while progress is rapid, one question remains central: what does it actually take to make Physical AI work in practice?

NVIDIA is building the compute platforms and simulation tools. ALLSIDES is building the 3D data layer and infrastructure.

Join Franz Tschimben (CEO, ALLSIDES) and Adam Brasic (Senior Solution Architect, NVIDIA) for a fireside chat and reality check on where Physical AI stands today, what is already working, and where real value is emerging.

The conversation will explore how simulation, infrastructure, and AI come together in real-world applications, and what it takes to turn Physical AI into a viable business. It will touch on platforms such as Omniverse and Isaac Sim, the role of high-quality 3D data, and why data is increasingly becoming the bottleneck in this space.

This is a curated gathering of founders, investors, developers, and researchers working at the intersection of AI and the physical world.

Fashion's been doing this for 20 years. Tech, welcome to the chat.

This is the direction tech is headed: AI writes the code, nobody maintains it, everyone rebuilds from scratch every six months. Custom tools nobody documented. Codebases that sprawl like a Shein cart. 
(Scott's take: https://worksonmymachine.ai/p/entering-technical-debts-zirp-era)

This is what fashion has been doing for twenty years: make it cheap, make it fast, make it disposable, make it again. A closet full of things you don't remember buying and a trillion dollars in returns and waste. (Nancy's take: https://repairera.substack.com/p/earth-month-is-a-trap)

The question is whether tech learns from fashion's mistake, or repeats it at a new scale.

This Tech Week, we're hosting a happy hour of guided roundtables across tech, fashion, ops, & sustainability. 

Expert hosts leading conversations on different angles of the theme. Everyone has a chance to bring their perspective. Topics like what fast fashion does right, what tech can learn from fashion (and vice versa), infrastructure nobody sees, and what "buy it for life" means in 2026.

Expect cross-industry collaboration, a few drinks, a few laughs, and maybe some insight on how to move forward.

Tech bros, fashion girlies, investors looking for the moat, and sustainability folks who saw this coming. 
All are welcome. 

Co-hosted by 
Nancy Rhodes (Alternew, The Repair Era) and 
Scott Werner (Artificial Ruby, Sublayer).

By registering, you'll be subscribed to Works on My Machine and The Repair Era. Consider it homework for the roundtable.
