What is HuCapital?

​​​​​​HuCapital is an AI social platform uniting entrepreneurial creatives and professionals through 1:1, peer group and prompted matches; powered by our Al Engine Huey. Learn more at hucapital.co.

About This Event

HuCapital is teaming up with New York Tech Week to bring together founders, builders, and tech professionals for a hands-on experience exploring AI and the Future of Work. This event blends insight and execution, starting with a fireside chat featuring investors and operators shaping the future of work, followed by a hands-on vibe coding session where attendees will actively build AI-powered solutions.

Attendees will collaborate in real time using tools like Lovable to prototype solutions that address real challenges across hiring, productivity, and access to opportunity in an evolving workforce.

This experience is designed to bring together people who are not only thinking about the future of work, but actively building it!

Key Takeaways

Understand What’s Fundable:
Learn what VCs are actually looking for in the future of work space and how to position AI-driven ideas to be investable and scalable.

See How AI Is Being Applied:
Gain real insight into how founders are using AI to solve challenges across hiring, productivity, and skill development.

Navigate the Shift in Hiring & Talent:
Understand how Talent and People leaders are adapting to AI-driven changes in workforce strategy, recruiting, and evaluation.

Leverage Community as a Competitive Advantage:
Explore how social capital, networks, and ecosystems are becoming key drivers of opportunity and career mobility.

Go From Idea to Prototype:
Learn how to quickly build and test ideas using vibe coding and AI tools, and walk away with something tangible.

Meet Our Speakers

Ash Straughn | Co-Founder & CEO, SAM

Ash is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sam, an AI-powered platform that places US-based, startup-experienced talent through flexible, subscription-based engagements. With 10+ years spanning operations, marketplace scaling, and startup infrastructure, including experience at Postmates and JPMorgan Chase, Ash brings a deep understanding of what companies need at every stage. At Sam, she drives company strategy, AI product development, GTM, and partnerships, with a clear mission: make Sam the default talent infrastructure built for how startups hire in an AI-first world.

Juju Fontaine | Founder & CEO, HuCapital

Jerlisa “Juju” Fontaine is the Founder & CEO of HuCapital, an AI-powered community platform uniting entrepreneurial creatives and professionals via 1:1, peer group, and prompted matches, all powered by AI superconnector Huey. Through HuCapital, Fontaine is on a mission to transform online connections into lasting IRL relationships that spark fruitful career, entrepreneurial, and collaborative opportunities for the next generation of leaders. Fontaine is also a seasoned product manager and tech leader with over a decade of experience in digital health and professional development, having worked on AI-powered career tools, health insurance engagement systems, SMS-based programs, chatbots, and optimized EHR software.

Jonaed Iqbal | Talent Acquisition Partner, Parola

Jonaed Iqbal is a Talent Acquisition Partner at Parola, Founder of NoDegree.com, and host of The NoDegree Podcast, where he interviews people without college degrees and shares their stories to help others follow similar paths to success. Jonaed has helped over 800 candidates, with clients landing jobs and interviews at companies including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Spotify, Tesla, TikTok, and Disney. He is committed to shattering the stigma that college is the only path to success.

Yanique Elliott | Founder & Venture Investor, Ambitious Global

Yanique is a Technologist, Entrepreneur, and Venture Investor with expertise in data privacy, risk management, operational strategy, VC due diligence, and career development. She has been recognized by Yahoo Finance as a Top 100 Future Leader and named among NYC’s Top 65 Inspiring Women in FinTech. Yanique is the Founder of Young Ambitious One (YAO), a career advancement platform helping job seekers, students, and professionals land their next roles. She is also the Founder & Managing Partner of Ambitious Global, an advisory services platform connecting businesses, entrepreneurs, and startups with leading advisors, capital, and resources for growth.

Boaz Descalo | Founder & CEO, Node8.ai

Boaz Descalo is an AI strategist, technologist, and Founder of Node8.ai, an AI advisory and implementation firm that helps companies design, build, and deploy production-ready AI systems. He also serves as an AI expert with Primary Venture Partners, is an Industry Advisor at Cornell Tech, and is a super-connector in the NYC AI startup ecosystem, building AI-first communities that connect founders, investors, and operators across the US.

Join SimpleClosure and Carta for an exclusive panel discussion on the future of law in the age of AI. Learn how artificial intelligence is reshaping the legal industry and redefining what's possible for startups and established firms alike. 

Featured speakers:
- Dori Yona – CEO, SimpleClosure
- Jesse Carey – Product Strategy & Ops, Stripe
- Sam Garcia – Partner, Amplo

Speaker bios:
Dori Yona
Dori started SimpleClosure after facing a tough moment in his own business when he needed help closing down a company but couldn't find good advice anywhere. After running an app called Earny that millions of people used, he knew there had to be a better way to help business owners close their companies. His new company, SimpleClosure, now helps hundreds of other business owners shut down their companies faster and cheaper than traditional methods. Based in Santa Monica with his family, Dori works to show that closing a business doesn't have to be scary or hard, and that learning from tough experiences can lead to helping others.

Jesse Carey
Jesse Carey leads growth for Stripe Atlas, Stripe’s startup incorporation platform. He previously served as Business Operations Lead at Headway, a mental health startup, where he launched the company’s government business. Prior, he was a Strategy & Planning Manager at Uber Eats and a management consultant focused on payments. He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School after attending Sydney Law School, having moved to the US from Australia in 2017.

Sam Garcia
Sam Garcia is a Partner with the Amplo platform of Collective Global. Sam focuses on the Seed/Series A practice at Amplo and serves on the boards of Lightyear, Flume, Kredi, Tradespace, Wizehire, Steno, Axion Ray, Doxel, and previously served on the board of Legalpad until they were acquired by Deel. Sam is a Lecturer at Harvard Law School where he teaches a course called Applying Legal Skills to VC Business Diligence. He also sits on the board of LatinxVC and serves as the organization’s Vice President. Sam is a graduate of the Business Honors Program at the University of Texas at Austin and holds a JD from Harvard Law School.

Who should attend:
- ECVC Lawyers looking to understand emerging trends
- Startup advisors and investors focused on legal services and compliance
- Anyone curious about how law is evolving with technology

Schedule:
Doors open at 8:30 AM for breakfast and coffee, followed by the panel discussion from 9:00 – 10:00. AM. Light networking to follow. 

About SimpleClosure: SimpleClosure is the shutdown partner for founders and startups navigating the less-talked-about side of entrepreneurship. When it’s time to properly close a company, SimpleClosure handles the paperwork, legal filings, compliance requirements, and final steps founders are often left to figure out on their own. What is traditionally a confusing, months-long process becomes a clearer path forward, so founders can close cleanly and move forward with confidence. To learn more, visit SimpleClosure.com.

Your AI & Product works. But does your user trust it?

Most founders optimize for capability. The best founders optimize for human experience. The difference is whether someone uses your product once or makes it part of their life.

In this 90-minute working session, we'll take a small group of product founders through the same process Tequity uses with its clients:
- Map the user's world — who they are, what they're doing when they encounter your product, and what they're feeling
- Identify the trust gaps — where your product asks users to make a leap of faith, and whether you've earned it
- Build a design brief — a one-page document that captures the decisions your product needs to make about how it presents itself to humans

This is hands-on. Bring your product (or your idea). You'll work on your own company with guidance from our team.

You'll leave with a design brief you can hand to your designer (or Claude), your dev team, or yourself — and start using immediately.

Who this is for: 
— Founders at the zero-to-one stage building AI products 
— Technical founders who know their product works but aren't sure it communicates well 
— Anyone who's gotten the feedback "the product is powerful but confusing"

Limited to 10 people so everyone gets individual attention.

Led by Design Labs at Tequity, a design and engineering studio that partners with early-stage startups. Design Labs has worked with 25+ 0-1 companies in 2025 alone that were born out of Harvard, Stanford and MIT - helping them find PMF. We also run a grant program where qualifying startups get credits covering 50% of their monthly design and engineering costs with us.

Coffee provided.

Bring Your Product. We'll Break It.

Live adversarial testing for 10 AI-native founders. 60 minutes. Real vulnerabilities. Coffee provided.

Your product ships fast. Your attackers move faster.

Most early-stage companies think security is something to solve later, after scale, after growth, after fundraising. But modern products are being probed from day one by bots, automated scripts, AI-assisted attackers, and increasingly sophisticated threat actors.

In this 60-minute live session, we’ll simulate how real attackers evaluate a product and show you where your system breaks before the internet does.

Using controlled offensive security methods, the Tequity Security Ops team will:

— Map your exposed attack surface across product, infrastructure, workflows, and user behavior
— Demonstrate how seemingly small vulnerabilities compound into major security risks
— Identify trust and security gaps across authentication, permissions, APIs, AI systems, internal tooling, and operational workflows
— Show how attackers think, move, escalate access, and exploit assumptions inside modern products
— Help you understand what security maturity actually looks like for a zero-to-one company

This is not a theoretical webinar. It is a live working session.

Bring your product, staging environment, prototype, or architecture. We’ll walk through real-world attack scenarios and show you where your company is most vulnerable today.

You’ll leave with:

* A high-level risk assessment of your current product ecosystem
* A practical understanding of your most critical vulnerabilities
* A security prioritization framework for your current stage
* Recommendations on what to fix immediately vs later
* A clearer picture of what modern Security Ops should look like inside a growing startup

Who this is for:
— Founders building AI-native or SaaS products
— Engineering teams moving quickly without dedicated security leadership
— Startups handling sensitive user, healthcare, fintech, or enterprise data
— Teams preparing for enterprise sales, compliance reviews, or due diligence
— Companies that have never undergone adversarial security testing before

Limited to 10 companies so each team gets hands-on attention.

Led by Tequity, an applied AI company, working with early-stage startups across AI, health-tech, fintech, and enterprise software. Our teams work closely with zero-to-one founders to build products that are not only usable and scalable, but resilient under real-world conditions.

Then try to replicate the movement from memory. The sensor will tell you if your correction went the right direction, if your pelvis compensated, and whether you held it correctly. Most people are humbled. All people get it.

Hear from the founder behind LumbarGuide — originally built to help adolescents with lumbar scoliosis practice rehabilitation exercises accurately at home using dual IMU sensors, it revealed something much more universal: most of us move through life with zero feedback on whether we're doing it right when the professionals aren’t around.

The startup org chart is breaking.

Founders are under pressure to move faster, stay leaner, and build more with less. But the old answer (hire a full executive team, add more headcount, and hope the org chart catches up) no longer works for most early-stage companies.

At the same time, two new forms of leverage are changing how startups operate: AI agents and senior fractional.

AI agents open up a nearly infinite set of opportunities to automate tasks, redesign workflows, monitor execution, and support day-to-day operations.

Fractional leaders give founders access to experienced operators across go-to-market, product, operations, finance, engineering, design, people, and strategy without the cost or commitment of premature full-time hires. 

But for early-stage founders, the hard part is knowing how to put those pieces together.

Which roles need senior human judgment? Which functions should be fractional before they become full-time? Which tasks are ready for agents? What should stay founder-led, what should be delegated to expert operators, and what should become an AI-enabled workflow?

This NY Tech Week session helps founders answer those questions.

Felix, the AI CEO of The Masinov Company, Build Momentum, and Founders & Fractionals will guide founders through a practical, hands-on session for redesigning the early-stage operating team around founder ownership, fractional talent, future full-time hires, and AI agents.

The program includes:

A quick demystification of AI agents for early-stage founders
What agents are, what they can realistically do today, where they are useful, and where the hype gets ahead of reality.

A focused discussion on building with fractional talent
How founders can access senior operators across key functions without overhiring too early, and how to scope fractional support around outcomes instead of vague advisory work.

An interactive operating team mapping exercise
Participants will identify the tasks, roles, workflows, and bottlenecks inside their business, then draft the ideal mix of founder ownership, fractional leaders, full-time hires, and AI agents.

• AI is making us less creative — not more

• AI companions will be a net positive for society
• Within 10 years, AI will make college degrees irrelevant

Alex Koshykov (https://www.linkedin.com/in/alex-koshykov/) is a co-founder of BeKey (https://bekey.io/) and a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, and promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/BeKey-Hub). Join us for an evening of drinks, networking, and a conversation the accounting profession is overdue for.

General-purpose AI is impressive. It can summarize, draft, and reason across an enormous range of tasks. But accounting and tax aren't general problems. They're governed by rules that change, edge cases that carry liability, and judgment calls that no model gets right just by being large. That gap, between what AI can do and what accounting actually demands, is where the most consequential work in the profession is happening right now.

This panel brings together thought leaders, firm leaders from the profession, and the builders working at that frontier to share what's working in practice, where the hype still outpaces reality, and what separates AI that holds up in an accounting environment from AI that doesn't.

If you're leading a firm or advising one, this is a conversation worth being in the room for.

partiful-h5aymfedr9tcz0cufgwx.description:
Strategic advantage has long rested on the quality of analysis: who could synthesize the most information, find the sharpest insight, and turn it into a defensible plan. AI has collapsed the cost and time of that work. Market intelligence that took six weeks now takes an afternoon, and is often stale by the time leadership convenes to discuss it.

This is not a productivity story. It is a structural one. When analysis is cheap, the activities that defined the strategist's role for fifty years (data gathering, framework application, deck construction) lose their economic value. What remains is judgment, narrative, political navigation, and the ability to commit an organization to action under uncertainty. Those skills are scarcer, harder to teach, and largely absent from how strategy talent is currently developed.

Join us on June 4 as this panel examines what that means for the people who buy strategy work, sell it, fund the firms disrupting it, and train the next generation expected to practice it.

Core Questions
What does decision-making look like at the speed of inference, and where does it break? How are PE operators and corporate boards repricing strategy services now that the underlying analytical labor has been commoditized? What is the new moat for consulting firms when generic models replicate most of a junior associate's output? If AI handles the apprenticeship work, how does the next generation of senior strategists develop the judgment AI cannot replicate? And where has this transformation underdelivered, and what are firms quietly walking back?

Panelists
● Jenny Fielding, Co-founder + Partner, Everywhere Ventures
● Kes Sampanthar, Founder & CEO, Centaurian AI
● David Thomson, Founder & CEO of Inevitable
● Iliya P. Zogovic, Founder & CEO, DBD Investment Bank
● Moderator Christine Alemany, Founder, Thrv Advisors (Women’s Circle Board Member)

partiful-x0u5grmzviutrjoaogvm.description:
If AI should read codebase structure rather than guess at it, why doesn't it?

AI coding tools work by reading source files and inferring architecture. The result is "almost-usable" code that requires manual refactoring. 

The deeper problem isn't the tools — it's that most frameworks weren't designed to be read structurally.  There's no layer for AI to reason against, so the tools are stuck guessing.

SpyneJS is an open-source framework designed for AI-assisted development.  It exposes a structural codemap that gives agents a deterministic understanding of application structure.

Refined over six years in enterprise environments, the framework is designed so generated code respects architectural boundaries from the first prompt.

Join us for a live demo of frontend codegen that holds up under peer review.  We'll show how agents interact with SpyneJS to produce structurally sound features, then discuss what becomes possible when the codebase itself functions as a working specification.

For developers, founders, and anyone evaluating where serious frontend development goes next.

spynejs.com

Born in Argentina more than 20 years ago, Ekoparty has become a key part of the country’s cybersecurity ecosystem and one of the most recognized community-driven platforms in Latin America. What started as a technical conference evolved into a space that connects researchers, startups, companies, founders, and emerging talent, helping showcase the depth of Argentina’s cybersecurity culture and technical expertise.

Today, Argentina represents one of the most distinctive cybersecurity ecosystems in the region, combining highly skilled professionals, a strong research and hacker culture, and a growing number of companies building globally competitive products and services. From independent researchers to established firms, the country has become an important source of innovation and talent for the international cybersecurity industry.

This session will explore how Argentina built this ecosystem, the role community platforms like Ekoparty played in fostering collaboration and visibility, and why the country has become a strategic opportunity for U.S. companies, investors, and organizations looking to connect with Latin American cybersecurity talent and innovation. It will also cover how Ekoparty expanded beyond Argentina to strengthen regional and international connections, including its recent launch in the United States with Ekoparty Miami.

Building AI Agents for Science: From Theory to Laboratory

Artificial intelligence is undergoing a paradigm shift, moving beyond simple chatbots to autonomous agents capable of complex reasoning. Nowhere is this transformation more critical than in the sciences, where AI agents are beginning to accelerate the pace of discovery, from drug development to material science.

Hosted by GRAIL, this session explores the "Autonomous Science" movement—a new frontier where PhD-level agents partner with researchers to automate the scientific loop. This two-part event features a high-level panel of academic and industry leaders followed by a hands-on technical workshop.

During the workshop, participants will be introduced to ApexClaw, GRAIL's flagship platform for building advanced science agents. Built on the open-source foundations of OpenClaw, ApexClaw provides the specialized reasoning and rigor required for scientific research.

What You’ll Learn
Participants will explore the architecture of scientific agents and the shift toward autonomous R&D, including:

#The Future of Research: A panel discussion with higher-education leaders and AI experts on how agents are reshaping the university lab.
#The Agentic Loop: Understanding how AI systems handle hypothesis generation, experimental planning, and data interpretation.
#Introduction to ApexClaw: How to leverage specialized frameworks to go beyond general-purpose LLMs.
#Live Implementation: A guided session on deploying your first autonomous agent for a scientific task.

Who Should Attend
This event is designed for:
#Founders and Researchers looking to integrate autonomous workflows into their R&D.
#PhD Students and Academics interested in the future of digital laboratory assistants.
#Engineers and Developers exploring the intersection of AI, OpenClaw, and specialized scientific domains.
#Investors interested in the "AI for Science" vertical.

What Participants Receive
All attendees will receive exclusive free credits for ApexClaw, allowing you to implement your own agent during the workshop and continue building your own digital researcher after the event concludes.

The location will be provided to registered attendees.

Duration
2-hour

​What happens when Lightning AI's frontier training infrastructure meets Validia's agent expertise?

​A hackathon where you build smarter, ship faster, and deploy agents in a secure manner.

​We're excited to host our second hackathon right here in Manhattan, where we'll challenge you and your team to build autonomous agents that work the way you work - faster than ever before.

​What You'll Build With:

​You'll have full access to two powerful resources working in tandem:

​Lightning AI Studios provides the infrastructure to build, train, and deploy your AI agents with the same tools used for frontier model development. Access to serious compute, seamless workflows, and OpenClaw - the framework for building personalized autonomous agents that understand your unique context and workflows.

​Validia's team brings deep expertise in the safety and security behind AI agents. We specialize in building detection for unsafe prompts, jailbreak attempts, and distillation attacks against your models.

​The Challenge:

​Build a personalized autonomous agent using Lightning AI's OpenClaw studio that adapts to how you and your team actually work — and does it safely. Your agent should solve a real problem and demonstrate what's possible when you combine cutting-edge AI infrastructure with genuine security built in from the ground up, not bolted on after the fact.

​Think: agents that learn from your unique work patterns, automate repetitive workflows specific to your domain, and orchestrate complex tasks — all while staying resilient against the threats that make real-world AI deployment risky. Can your agent handle adversarial inputs without breaking? Does it know when it's being manipulated or probed? Can it maintain context about how you operate without leaking sensitive information or being distilled by a bad actor?

​The best submissions won't just be the most capable agents. They'll be the ones that are hardest to break.

partiful-hi6tdz9djtmb6zrpz9zs.description:
We’re deploying AI agents faster than we can verify them. Ezio is changing that narrative.

As AI agents take on increasingly consequential roles, the question of trust has never been more urgent. What does it actually mean to trust AI agents and how do you build responsible infrastructure? Trust in AI agents is still largely improvised - based on intuition, brand, or retrospective debugging - rather than something measurable, inspectable, and enforced at the system level.

We’re convening the best group of leading VCs, founders, academics, and product leaders in New York to explore a core question: what does it truly mean to trust AI systems - and what would it take to build a reliable trust layer around them? Through a focused panel and small-group roundtables, we’ll move beyond surface-level conversations and examine questions like:

-How should we evaluate agents that plan, reason, and take multi-step actions?
-What does reliability mean in systems that evolve across tool use, memory, and environment?
-Where are the current blind spots in agent evaluation, monitoring, and control?
-What signals - technical or behavioral - could make agent trustworthiness observable in real time?

Grounded in lessons from high-stakes domains like finance and healthcare - where risk is modeled, audited, and continuously monitored - we’ll explore how similar principles might translate (or fail to translate) to modern AI systems. Topics will include hallucination and bias detection, evaluation blind spots, human-in-the-loop design, and emerging approaches to quantifying model reliability.

There is “responsible AI” as a principle. But this is a working session on something more concrete: how to move from intuition-based trust to system-level guarantees - and what needs to exist, technically and institutionally, for that shift to happen.
partiful-hi6tdz9djtmb6zrpz9zs.ogTitle: AI Agents in the Wild: A Candid Conversation on Trust and Accountability - #NYTechWeek | Partiful

​Building your sales and marketing systems can feel overwhelming. These office hours are an opportunity to ask questions, troubleshoot challenges, and get practical advice on how to grow your startup.

​Join Kat Rucker, Fractional VP of Sales and Marketing, for small-group office hours focused on early-stage go-to-market strategy.

​Common topics include:

​• Founder-led sales
• Building early pipeline and outreach
• Messaging and positioning
• Turning conversations into revenue
• Prioritizing sales and marketing when you have limited time and resources

​Bring your current questions or challenges, and we’ll work through them together.

​How the Sessions Work
​These are small group office hours designed to keep the discussion practical and interactive.

Host will message you with a recommended 15- minute time slot during the hour, but feel free to come and go as you please.

​Each time block functions as drop-in group office hours, so you’re welcome to join for the full session or come with a specific question.

​About Kat
​Kat Rucker is the founder of Kat Rucker Consulting Group and a Fractional VP of Sales who works with early-stage startups on go-to-market strategy, sales systems, and founder-led growth.

​She has over 10 years of experience in B2B sales across software and services and helps startups build their first scalable revenue processes.

Kat's LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/kat-rucker/
